name: SDF morph
description: A mass of liquid chrome morphing through sphere, cube, octahedron and torus while five satellites orbit into it on tilted paths and are absorbed. The morph mixes the distance functions rather than cross-fading two renders, so the solid genuinely passes through the shapes in between — and it is a mirror, so the strip lights around the horizon sweep across it and one reflection bounce carries the satellites curved across the core. Beats leave a ripple travelling out through the surface.

morph.description: Position through the four primitives, wrapping every 1.0. Bound to `phrase` by default, so the core completes one full circuit of the shapes every four bars and the morph lands on the music instead of drifting against it.

blend.description: Smooth-minimum radius. Higher makes the satellites melt into the core sooner; driven by bass it pulls the whole group together on every kick. Past about 0.5 everything is one lump and the morph underneath it stops being legible.

spread.description: Orbit radius of the satellites. Low values keep them permanently inside the core and there is nothing to absorb.

warp.description: Twist applied to the space everything lives in, so the satellites bend along the same curve as the core. Past ~0.9 the field overstates distances badly enough that the marcher steps through the surface.

ripple.description: Shockwave travelling out through the surface. This is the surface itself answering the music rather than just its brightness.

glow.description: The aura gathered around the mass on the way in.

steps.description: March steps. The main cost lever — drop this first if the render rate suffers. Twisted space needs more of them than a plain field does.
